challenges.title: Match the word cat
challenges.task: Write a pattern that matches the string cat and nothing else. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: A pattern made only of letters matches exactly those letters.

challenges.title: A three-digit number
challenges.task: Match strings made of exactly three digits, such as 007 or 123. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: \d matches one digit. Say how many with {n}.

challenges.title: Cat or dog
challenges.task: Match either the string cat or the string dog. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: The | symbol means or.

challenges.title: Colour, either spelling
challenges.task: Match color and colour (American and British spelling). The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: ? makes the character before it optional.

challenges.title: Pull out every number
challenges.task: Write a pattern so that re.findall returns every whole number in the text, as strings.
challenges.hint: One or more digits: \d with a + after it.

spec.text: Order 66 shipped on day 12 with 3 boxes at 450 grams.

challenges.title: A hex colour code
challenges.task: Match a # followed by exactly six hex digits (0-9, a-f, A-F), like #1a2B3c. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: Build a set with [0-9a-fA-F]. The # needs no escape.

challenges.title: Words ending in -ing
challenges.task: Make findall return every word that ends in ing (the word can have any letters before it).
challenges.hint: \b marks a word edge, \w+ is a run of word characters.

spec.text: Running and jumping are fun, but sing, ring and king are short. Walking is slow.

challenges.title: US ZIP code, with optional +4
challenges.task: Match five digits, optionally followed by a hyphen and four more digits: 90210 or 90210-1234. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: Put the hyphen-and-four-digits in a group, then make the whole group optional with ?.

challenges.title: A username
challenges.task: Match 3 to 16 characters: letters, digits or underscores, and the first one must be a letter. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: One letter first, then {2,15} more word characters.

challenges.title: Text inside quotes
challenges.task: Make findall return what is inside each pair of double quotes, without the quote marks.
challenges.hint: A group around the middle makes findall return only the group. Add ? after the repeat so it stops at the first closing quote.

spec.text: She said "hello" and then "goodbye" before leaving.

challenges.title: Collapse the spaces
challenges.task: Write a pattern so that re.sub(pattern, ' ', text) turns every run of spaces and tabs into one space.
challenges.hint: \s matches any whitespace character; + means one or more.

challenges.title: A 24-hour time
challenges.task: Match HH:MM with two-digit hours 00-23 and minutes 00-59, like 09:45. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: Hours are [01]\d or 2[0-3]: put that alternation in a group. Minutes are [0-5]\d.

challenges.title: A date, YYYY-MM-DD
challenges.task: Match a date with a four-digit year, a month 01-12 and a day 01-31. (It does not need to know which months are short.) The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).

challenges.title: Split dates into parts
challenges.task: Make findall return, for every date in the text, a list of its [year, month, day].
challenges.hint: Put each part in its own group: with several groups findall returns a tuple per match.

challenges.title: Doubled words
challenges.task: Make findall return each word that is accidentally repeated twice in a row, once per repeat.
challenges.hint: Capture a word with (\w+), then refer back to it with \1. Add \b so you match whole words.

spec.text: This is is a test of the the system, not not a drill.

challenges.title: Swap Last, First
challenges.task: Write a pattern so that re.sub(pattern, r'\2 \1', text) turns every Lovelace, Ada into Ada Lovelace.
challenges.hint: Two groups, one for each name, with the comma and space between them.

challenges.title: A password rule
challenges.task: Match any string of 8 or more characters that contains at least one digit and at least one uppercase letter. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: Use two lookaheads at the start, each looking ahead for one requirement: (?=.*\d) and (?=.*[A-Z]). Then match the characters with .{8,}.

challenges.title: Prices after a dollar sign
challenges.task: Make findall return just the number of each price (not the $). Prices may have cents.
challenges.hint: A lookbehind (?<=\$) checks for the $ without including it. Use (?:...) for any group you do not want findall to return.

spec.text: Pens cost $4.50, notebooks $12, and a bag is $120.99 (not 15 percent).

challenges.title: Lines without the word error
challenges.task: Match any line that does not contain the lowercase word error anywhere. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: A negative lookahead (?!...) at the start can forbid something later in the string: (?!.*error).

challenges.title: Severe log lines
challenges.task: The text is a log with one entry per line. Make findall return the level (ERROR or WARN) of each entry that has one. The MULTILINE flag is already on, so ^ matches at the start of every line.
challenges.hint: Anchor with ^, skip the date and time with \S+ \S+, then capture (ERROR|WARN).

challenges.title: An IPv4 address
challenges.task: Match four numbers from 0 to 255 separated by dots, with no leading zeros (so 192.168.1.1 but not 192.168.01.1). The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: One octet is 25[0-5] or 2[0-4]\d or 1\d\d or [1-9]?\d. Write it once, then repeat: (octet\.){3} followed by one more octet. Use (?:...) groups.

challenges.title: An email address (good enough)
challenges.task: Match a simple email address: a name (letters, digits, and . _ + -), an @, then a domain with at least one dot. The whole string must match (the page uses re.fullmatch).
challenges.hint: [\w.+-]+ before the @; after it, a label then one or more (\.label). Remember to escape the dot.
